record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: Why should social-resilience models consider each agent’s social impact, and how can that impact be quantified? The question should include how an agent’s total impact can combine its own importance with support or opposition received from others through weighted signed relations.

evidence.quote: Questions • Why do we consider the social impact of agents? How can we quantify it?
What matters in an organization is not just the importance, ri, but also the support or opposition an agent receives from others. Their inﬂuences are combined in an individual social impact, Ii.
Here, we deﬁne the social impact as Ii = ∑j wij rj = Ip i − In i . The wij denote the weighted and signed relations between agents, which can be positive, negative or zero.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite set of agents $\{1,2,\dots,N\}$, where each agent $i$ has an intrinsic importance $r_i \in \mathbb{R}$ and is connected to other agents through weighted, signed relations $w_{ij} \in \mathbb{R}$ (which may be positive, negative, or zero, representing support, opposition, or absence of influence, respectively). Define the social impact of agent $i$ as
$$I_i \;=\; \sum_{j} w_{ij}\, r_j \;=\; I_i^{p} - I_i^{n},$$
where $I_i^{p} = \sum_{j:\, w_{ij} r_j > 0} w_{ij} r_j$ aggregates supportive influences and $I_i^{n} = -\sum_{j:\, w_{ij} r_j < 0} w_{ij} r_j$ aggregates opposing influences.

Address the following:
(a) Provide a principled justification for why models of social resilience should incorporate such an individual social impact $I_i$ rather than relying solely on the intrinsic importance $r_i$.
(b) Develop a quantification scheme for $I_i$ that combines an agent's own importance with the support and opposition received from others through the weighted signed relations $w_{ij}$, and discuss how the decomposition into $I_i^{p}$ and $I_i^{n}$ captures the qualitative effects of antagonistic versus cooperative ties on collective social resilience.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a conceptual modeling question about how to define and justify a notion of individual social impact within social-resilience frameworks. A standard definition $I_i=\sum_j w_{ij} r_j$ is in widespread use (going back to social impact theory by Latané and Nowak–Szamrej–Latané), but no canonical answer exists for which formulation is optimal in resilience modeling; it remains an open modeling problem.

status_evidence.title: Social impact theory / Nowak-Szamrej-Latané model
status_evidence.snippet: Social impact is quantified by summing weighted influences from other agents, separated into supportive and opposing components.
status_evidence.claim: A weighted-sum quantification of social impact with signed influences is a standard, though not unique, formulation.
